reason: The passage depicts Moses, functioning as a religious leader and prophet, as the supreme human authority. He alone receives God's word directly and serves as the exclusive intermediary between God and the people. When the people fear God's voice, they request Moses speak to them instead—affirming his superior role. The text explicitly states Israel will become a 'kingdom of priests' (mamlechet kohanim), establishing religious function as central to the nation's identity. The people solemnly covenant to obey all of God's words transmitted through Moses. Even Aaron, though also a religious figure, is subordinate to Moses and is shown capitulating to the people's pressure. Religious authority clearly supersedes other forms of human authority in this covenant narrative.
